newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs to correct down to 126.37 and below.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs to correct down to 126.37 and below.

text.p: LIFFE June BTP futures will be limited to the upside as they continue to correct down to 126.37 and beyond on Wednesday, technical analysts said.

"BTPs are moving away from the 129.02/05 recent top. They will continue correcting the recent run up and any gains will be capped with moves down to 126.37 and then 126.00/05," said Mike Macdonald, technical analyst at 4CAST in London.
He said the 126.37 level was a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the rally in the first half of April and should prove strong for the moment.
At 0743 GMT, June BTP futures were at 127.33, down 0.01.
On the way to 126.73, Macdonald saw some initial support at 126.73, Tuesday's low, and further interim levels around 126.50 to 126.50
Those levels reflect the daily lows on April 8 and 9.
"If it breaks below 126.37, then 126.00, 05 is the early April break area," he said.

The contract climbed higher to find a new trading range moving from 124.88 to 126.05 on April 4, and from 126.00 to 127.70 on April 7. Marc Ostwald, techncial strategist at Monument Derivatives said overall, the tone of BTPs was still poor.
He said BTPs could drift back to key support around 127.00.
"The 126.97 level is a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the whole move up from the lower levels, so there will be reasonable suport there," Ostwald said.
Under 126.97, he also cited 126.50 and 126.56 on the way to 126.32, a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the same rally.
"That area should support it and from there there is scope to build a better bounce," he said.
But Ostwald said the high correlation between the lira/mark rate and BTPs meant that unless the currency moved considerably BTPs were not likely to make much upside.
To the upside, Macdonald said there was immediate resistance at Tuesday's high of 127.55, with minor congestion above there centred around 128.00.
Ostwald saw the potential for BTPs to move slightly higher.
"If we can break through 127.55,60 we could have a bit of a bounce to 128.13, 15 - the low last Thursday and the high on Monday respectively," Ostwald said.
At the short end June Eurolira futures were at 93.14, down two basis points from Tuesday's close.
